_comment: Manifest economy rules. Shared by the bot simulator now and the game server later. Money is in game credits; distance is in map units; time is in hours.

machinery._comment: Valuable and scarce: depth 0.1 means a port's market is a tenth the size of grain's, so a 100-unit load moves the price a lot and the same lane stops paying quickly. 100 units cost more than the 10,000 start cash, so early on cash decides the load.

markets._comment: Each port holds a stock of each commodity. Price slides from ceiling (empty) to floor (stock at twice the target). Producer ports add stock every hour; consumer ports remove it. Production and consumption scale with the number of companies (companies / reference_companies, at least min_scale), so each company sees a similar share of trade whatever the player count. All market sizes (production, consumption, target and maximum stock) are multiplied by a scale fixed for the season: (expected companies / reference_companies) ^ scale_exponent, at least min_scale (tuned by simulation: 0.5 at 30 companies, 0.72 at 100, 1 at 300). That keeps each company's share of trade the same at any player count.
markets._start_comment: Each season opens with ports that only produce a good stocked at target x (1 + start_spread) and ports that only consume it at target x (1 - start_spread). With every port at the target, prices were equal everywhere and no trade paid for the first ~6 days (hour 134 with 30 bots). 0.2 makes trade pay from hour one; simulated money change stays within -1.9% to +0.3% a day at 30, 100 and 300 companies.

information._comment: If true, every port shows how much cargo is already sailing towards it, so players can avoid piling onto the same route.

difficulty._comment: World difficulty, chosen on the admin page or with the DIFFICULTY env when a world or season starts. Each preset sets tax, port fee and upkeep for everyone, and botMinProfit: the smallest profit a bot trip must clear, which leaves the smaller margins for players; and botError: how far off (as a fraction, either way) each bot's guess of a sale price can be, so bots pick imperfect routes and sometimes lose money. Simulated season (players checking in every 4 hours, 30-60 bots): easy, players finish around 31,000-35,000 vs about 17,500 on normal; money grows 0.9-1.3%/day on easy vs 0.5-0.9% on normal (a little inflation, accepted by Dave).

ship._comment: This is the freighter (the starting ship); other classes are in ship_types. Upkeep applies to every ship after the first, so a broke company can always keep sailing. Companies in debt scrap an idle spare ship for half its price.

ship_types._comment: Ship classes a company can buy. freighter must match `ship` (the starting ship). Coaster: fast, small, cheap, thirsty per unit of cargo. Bulker: slow, big, dear, but moves the most cargo per fuel. Upkeep is the Normal-difficulty figure; it scales with the difficulty preset in the same ratio as the freighter's (Easy x0.75, Hard x1.25). A company's upkeep is the total for its ships minus one freighter's worth (the old 'first ship is free'), so a single coaster or freighter costs nothing to keep.

health_checks._comment: Thresholds the simulator reports against. Breaching one means the economy needs tuning.
